strings.name: Richard Sutton
strings.summary: Moving from psychology to computing, Sutton worked with adviser Andrew Barto on learning from rewards and experience, developing temporal-difference methods and co-authoring a major textbook. A longtime Alberta professor, he also worked with DeepMind. He and Barto received the 2024 Turing Award in 2025. In 2026 he co-founded Oak Lab to explore continual learning.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; reviewed November 15, 2026. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Made foundational contributions to reinforcement-learning theory and algorithms; his textbook and research influenced generations of AI researchers.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Toledo, Ohio, United States; published birth years differ between 1957 and 1958.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Stanford psychology BA (1978); University of Massachusetts Amherst computer-science PhD (1984).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Reinforcement-learning foundations
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Barto and others, studied learning from environmental feedback.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Textbook and dissemination
strings.highlights.h2.text: Co-authored Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction with Barto.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Co-founded Oak Lab

strings.timeline.t3.title: The Bitter Lesson

strings.timeline.t7.title: Temporal-difference research

strings.timeline.t8.title: Doctorate
